correctness.rationale: On the nonnegative competitive LV orthant, a hyperbolic sink must have positive supported abundance, positive-definite symmetric supported interaction matrix, and strictly negative invasion exponents. For alpha<1 an occupied peripheral pair must contain both leaves (otherwise missing sibling invades); for alpha>1 both cannot coexist by the negative eigenvalue 1-alpha. Without hub, every pair must be occupied; hub invasion threshold is beta=(1+alpha)/(2k) or beta=1/k. With hub, beta>1 forbids all leaves by indefinite principal minor, and beta<1 forces each pair occupied, giving explicit arrowhead-supported abundances h=(1-k beta)/(1-k beta^2), y=(1-beta)/(1-k beta^2), or all-leaf symmetric formula with 1+alpha replacing pair degree. Positivity and definiteness coincide with the stated open chambers; no unlisted supports. Independently solved rational support tests for k=2,3 at alpha=1/2,3/2 and beta=.1,.4,.5,1.3, yielding stable counts 1,1,2,8,8,9 as appropriate. The infinite classification rests on support argument, not finite tests.

value.rationale: A friendship graph is an elementary but natural motif for multistable competitive communities: one shared species interacting with k otherwise separated rival pairs. The classification locates real bifurcation boundaries between coexistence, exclusion, hub-only and bistability, and gives exact abundances and sink multiplicities for every k. More than generic clique counting; usable exact case study with experimentally meaningful finite competition strengths, without claiming basins or transition curve dynamics.

limitations: Hyperbolic local sink classes only, equality/transition lines excluded.
Known clique-exclusion theory is prior; no claim to general multistability.
